claim: Foot Locker closed its Avignon city-centre store on rue des Marchands on Tuesday 15 Sept 2026. Employees describe it as FL's first store in France. The 4 staff stay in the group at other stores. FL keeps Mistral 7 and Aushopping Avignon Nord.
data_point: Closure 2026-09-15 (after the 8/1/26 count date); 4 employees redeployed; 2 Avignon stores remain
source_name: Le Mag Avignon (citing Le Dauphiné Libéré 2026-09-11)
original_quote: Foot Locker fermera définitivement sa boutique du centre-ville d'Avignon mardi 15 septembre ... Les quatre salariées de cette boutique ne quitteront pas le groupe ... La boutique de la rue des Marchands était, d'après ses employées, la première implantation française de l'enseigne.
english_translation: Foot Locker will permanently close its Avignon city-centre shop on Tuesday 15 September ... The four employees will not leave the group ... According to its employees, the rue des Marchands shop was the brand's first French location.
verifier_note: Page fetched; it is dated 11 Sept 2026, and the closure date, 4 staff, the 2 remaining stores and the 'first in France' line are all present. It cites ledauphine.com (paywalled, not fetched). This is the only named closure in the set that firmly falls after 8/1/26. Google Maps still shows the store open, which illustrates how Google lags.

claim: The union ELA confirms Foot Locker closed its 'flagship' store in Max Center, Barakaldo (Bizkaia). The store employed 12 people. The deal agreed: no forced exits, all departures voluntary, severance equal to unfair dismissal.
data_point: 12 workers; voluntary exits only; severance at the 'despido improcedente' rate (33 days/yr under Spanish law, analyst gloss); Google Maps closed, last review 2025-12-16
original_quote: Cierran la tienda insignia de Foot Locker en el Centro Comercial Max Center donde trabajan 12 personas. Gracias al acuerdo, no habrá salidas forzosas.
english_translation: They are closing Foot Locker's flagship store in the Max Center shopping centre, where 12 people work. Thanks to the agreement, there will be no forced exits.
verifier_note: Page fetched; dated 09/02/2026; the quote, the 12 workers and the terms (voluntary exits, severance equal to despido improcedente) are verbatim. ELA's Facebook post corroborates it, and Google Maps flags Kareaga s/n Local B30-B31 permanently closed. The 33 days/yr figure is the analyst's reading of Spanish law and does not appear on the page.

claim: Foot Locker left the Centre Bourse mall (Marseille 1er) at end-2025, alongside Sephora (31 Dec) and after Galeries Lafayette (15 Nov). A Google review dated 2025-11-07 says the store was closing permanently because FNAC is taking the unit.
data_point: Closure ~Oct-Dec 2025 (Q4 FY25, post-deal); unit now covered by an advertising poster; Google review says FNAC is the incoming tenant
original_quote: Après la fermeture définitive des Galeries Lafayette le 15 novembre, Sephora et Foot Locker ont baissé le rideau au Centre Bourse (1er). ... Juste à côté, Foot Locker a également disparu du centre commercial au profit d'une grande affiche publicitaire.
english_translation: After the permanent closure of Galeries Lafayette on 15 November, Sephora and Foot Locker have pulled down the shutters at Centre Bourse (1st arr.). ... Right next door, Foot Locker has also disappeared from the shopping centre, replaced by a large advertising poster.
verifier_note: Article fetched (paywalled after the lede); it is dated 07/01/26 and the quote is present. The Google Maps pin 'FOOT LOCKER FRANCE 5397 CENTRE BOURSE' is flagged closed, with a review dated 2025-11-07 about FNAC arriving. The FNAC takeover rests on one consumer review and is unverified.
